label: Capitalism is contested and definitionally plural
text: The entry treats capitalism as a disputed concept with competing economic, social-order, and disciplinary definitions.
assumptions: The entry is selective and aimed at normative philosophy
Different definitions may not describe the same object
falsifier: Show that the alleged definitions converge on one necessary and sufficient core.

label: Marx: accumulation depends on wage labor and private control
text: Capitalism is a historically specific social relation in which private control of production, wage labor, commodity exchange, and accumulation form a reinforcing structure.
assumptions: Labor theory of value
Workers lack independent access to subsistence
Competition compels accumulation
falsifier: Find a capitalist regime with the specified wage/property/exchange structure but without the alleged accumulation dynamic, or a non-capitalist regime with the same structure.

label: Weber: capitalist durability is culturally motivated
text: Modern capitalism is sustained by an internalized cultural spirit, historically linked to Protestant work and saving, rather than by material relations alone.
assumptions: Cultural internalization causes durable accumulation
The Roman case is a meaningful comparison
falsifier: Demonstrate comparable capitalist accumulation without the proposed cultural mechanism, or the mechanism without capitalist accumulation.

label: Schumpeter: entrepreneurship drives creative destruction
text: Risk-taking entrepreneurs combine factors of production and drive recurring innovation that displaces older methods and values.
assumptions: Entrepreneurial agency is analytically distinct from competition
Innovation produces both abundance and social fatigue
falsifier: Compare innovation regimes with and without entrepreneurial coordination while holding capital, labor, and technology constant.

label: Hayek/Friedman: free markets and property yield efficiency
text: Private property and relatively unfettered markets coordinate dispersed information, promote preference satisfaction, and protect economic or political freedom.
assumptions: Prices aggregate relevant information
Exchange is sufficiently voluntary
Political power is decentralized rather than concentrated
falsifier: A planner, regulated market, or alternative ownership regime must outperform the market on the specified efficiency/freedom metric under comparable conditions.

label: Institutions constitute markets rather than merely constrain them
text: Property rights, rule of law, and political institutions are prerequisites of capitalist markets and their healthy operation.
assumptions: Institutional rules are constitutive rather than external
The relevant institutions can be specified and compared
falsifier: Identify a functioning capitalist market with no legal-political institutional substrate, or show institutions are irrelevant to its performance.

label: Polanyi: land, labor, and money are fictitious commodities
text: Generalized markets require state-mediated commodification of things not originally produced as commodities, which generates social countermovements.
assumptions: Commodification requires political action
Market exposure produces recurring protective responses
falsifier: Find generalized market exchange without state-mediated commodification or without the predicted countermovement.

label: Keynes: investment depends on uncertain expectations and liquidity preference
text: Investment and economic reproduction depend on expectations, money, credit, and the choice between productive investment and liquid assets.
assumptions: Liquidity preference is systematically underproductive
Money is not reducible to a neutral medium
falsifier: Show that investment is governed independently of expectations/liquidity, or that liquidity preference does not affect reproduction under relevant conditions.

label: Markets can raise welfare and benefit the worst off
text: Competitive markets and division of labor can maximize wealth, with sufficient redistribution or growth reaching everyone, including the worst off.
assumptions: Growth translates into broad welfare gains
The comparison class includes viable alternatives
falsifier: A comparable non-market arrangement produces greater welfare for the worst off, or growth systematically fails to reach them.

label: Markets process dispersed information more effectively than planners
text: Market prices and decentralized exchange can coordinate information that no central planner can fully possess.
assumptions: Relevant information is distributed
Price signals are not systematically distorted
Coordination is the correct objective
falsifier: A non-market institution consistently coordinates the same dispersed information better at comparable cost.

label: Market exchange is voluntary and protects negative liberty
text: Markets minimize coercive interference and allow individuals to pursue their own ends.
assumptions: Formal consent tracks substantive freedom
Workers have reasonable alternatives
falsifier: Show systematic coercion, domination, or lack of meaningful exit within otherwise voluntary market contracts.

label: Economic freedom disperses political power
text: Separating economic and political power helps protect political freedom and expression.
assumptions: Economic wealth remains sufficiently dispersed
Private power does not capture political institutions
falsifier: Show that capitalist economic concentration predictably undermines the fair value of political liberty.

label: Capitalism exploits labor through surplus extraction
text: Capitalist production extracts value from workers under conditions that may be unequal, unfair, or disrespectfully advantage-taking.
assumptions: The surplus is not justified as rent or entrepreneurial input
Workers lack meaningful alternatives
The relevant account of wrongness is specified
falsifier: Show that workers have genuine alternatives and that the residual is justified by a fair account of productive contribution, or reject the proposed wrong-making condition.

label: Capitalism structurally dominates workers or producers
text: Ownership and market dependence can give employers, capitalists, or impersonal market forces unilateral or arbitrary power over productive activity and subsistence.
assumptions: Domination requires meaningful exit/control
The locus is interactional, structural, dependent, or impersonal
falsifier: Demonstrate reciprocal control, meaningful exit, and non-arbitrary governance across the relevant employment or market relation.

label: Capitalism commodifies and destabilizes social reproduction/nature
text: Market organization depends on care, nature, and political institutions while representing them as autonomous or commodifiable, producing recurring social resistance and ecological strain.
assumptions: Dependence is necessary and systemic rather than accidental
The costs are normatively objectionable
falsifier: Show that capitalist reproduction can be sustained without the alleged externalized care/nature/political supports or that the supports are not harmed.

label: Capitalism has endogenous crisis or self-undermining tendencies
text: Capitalist dynamics can undermine the conditions of their own functioning through accumulation, financial instability, unemployment, or underinvestment.
assumptions: The system's proper function is independently specified
The tendency is systematic rather than episodic
falsifier: Show robust counterexamples across capitalist regimes, or specify a stable mechanism that prevents the predicted failure.

label: Welfare-state capitalism cannot secure justice
text: Large private inequalities can undermine fair opportunity, political equality, reciprocity, and self-respect even when a social minimum is guaranteed.
assumptions: Wealth converts into political influence
The inequality is institutional rather than contingent
Justice requires more than a floor
falsifier: Show a welfare-state capitalist arrangement that preserves fair opportunity, political equality, reciprocity, and self-respect despite large private inequality.

label: Critiques must establish distinctiveness, causality, systematicity, and perhaps non-contingency
text: A critique of capitalism is stronger when it shows the defect is distinctive to capitalism, caused by it, systematic, and not merely contingent.
assumptions: Capitalism has a stable target definition
The standards of critique are accepted
falsifier: Show the alleged defect occurs independently of capitalism, or that the critique standards exclude influential critiques without good reason.
